text:
Anya R: did a quick tiling/occupancy sweep for the fused+paged attention path (FlashAlt variant). ran micro-benchmarks on a p4d instance with smem=48k, tile_h=8/16/32, pipeline=2/3, batch=4/8. seeing a strange regression at seq=512 for tile_h=8 pipeline=3 (~11% throughput drop vs baseline).
Matt P: can you paste the bench output and the profiler summary? even a short snippet helps.
Anya R: sure — here's the minimal run and the summary I grabbed:
```bash
# run
./bench_attn --model=llama-7b --variant=flashalt-a --seq=512 --batch=8 --tile_h=8 --pipeline=3 --smem=48k
```
```
throughput tok/s:  1820  (baseline 2050)
avg latency ms:    42.7  (baseline 39.2)
SM L1/Shared Util: 78% / 91%
DRAM BW avg:       420 GB/s (peak 540)
smem spills:  2.3% ops
kv-cache read miss rate: 0.9% (small but correlated)
```
Anya R: nvprof snapshot (top counters):
```
dram_read_throughput: 420GB/s
achieved_occupancy: 0.78
local_shared_bank_conflicts: 0.06
warp_execution_efficiency: 0.88
```
Lee C: :thinking: odd that DRAM BW is that high while occupancy is only 0.78. pipeline=3 might be increasing register pressure and forcing more warp serialization. tile_h=8 increases kernel launch count which can inflate global traffic. have you tried tile_h=16 / pipeline=2?
Anya R: I tried tile_h=16 pipeline=2 quickly — throughput jumped to 1985 tok/s (only ~3% below baseline). smem spills dropped to 0.4% and DRAM BW to 360 GB/s.
Sam K: nice. can you include the exact perf matrix (tile_h x pipeline x batch) in a follow-up? i want to feed it into the autotuner. also, kv-cache thrash — are we invalidating or evicting too aggressively between batches?
Anya R: good call. I observed KV cache eviction spikes coinciding with small batches where batch<active_streams. likely our batch packing heuristic is causing premature cache flush. repro log: 
```
[2027-11-12T14:22:11Z] batch_pack: 3 streams -> created 5 kernels -> kv_evictions=12
[2027-11-12T14:22:11Z] kv_cache: evict_ratio=0.18
```
Lee C: if evictions align with pipeline depth, the KV spills will force DRAM reads that amplify BW. Two quick experiments: (1) prefer fewer kernels per request (merge small streams) (2) cap pipeline for seq>=256 when tile_h<=8.
Matt P: also consider changing kernel selection policy: pick the lower-pipeline kernel for seq>=512 when measured DRAM BW > 400GB/s. can we add a simple rule to the routing layer to fallback to tile_h=16/pipeline=2 variant?
Anya R: I'll push a tiny config flag and run the full sweep overnight. experiment ids: exp/fused-paged/sweep/1845601234-01..08. posting matrix tomorrow.
infra-bot: scheduled perf-run exp/fused-paged/sweep/1845601234-01 on runner p4d-11 for 2027-11-13T02:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
Sam K: awesome, thanks. if the autotuner picks the fewer-kernel packing we should see both lower DRAM BW and improved tail latency. :thumbsup:
Anya R: yep — will follow up with numbers and a quick diff for the kernel chooser rule.
Matt P: great, thx. if it still reproduces, we should add a regression test to eng-runtime CI with seq=512, batch=8 so we catch it early.
Lee C: agreed. low-effort CI guard will save a lot of debugging later.
Anya R: adding ticket and CI PR after the sweep.
